articles.title_orig: Etsy to restrict AI-generated content in effort to combat seller slop
articles.title_zh: Etsy to restrict AI-generated content in effort to combat seller slop
articles.content_orig:
Etsy announced new restrictions Thursday on AI-generated content on its platform, saying it threatens the integrity of its sellers’ work and leaves buyers exposed to fraud.
Among the new stipulations:
AI-generated art can still be sold on the platform as long as merchants “Play a clear role in what they create and are transparent about the process,” Etsy said in a note to sellers .
“Our marketplace only works when buyers and sellers trust each other,” Etsy Vice President of Customer Operations James Ossman wrote in a blog post .
“Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it. We know we have work to do to uphold this standard on Etsy.”
Etsy hosts more than 5 million entrepreneurs, most of whom are women who run one-person businesses out of their homes, according to an annual company report.
That distinguishes it from other major e-commerce platforms like Amazon and eBay, though it commands a fraction of those platforms’ revenues. As of 2024, Etsy hosted $10.9 billion-worth of goods’ sales, compared with about $75 billion for eBay and more than $700 billion for Amazon.
Some buyers responded positively to Etsy’s announcement.
“I can’t explain how infuriating it has been to purchase a crochet pattern, only to open the PDF and realize it’s fully AI-generated, doesn’t make sense, and definitely doesn’t match what the finished product should be,” creator Kara Lynne said on X .
The dawn of advanced AI has led to an explosion in AI-generated sales content — and a growing backlash from consumers against what they see as AI slop.
A recent social media trend among cafes and restaurants saw owners pledging not to use AI after egregious examples of AI-generated food images in the wild were shared on social media.
Major platforms are responding to the growing discontent. Many, including Facebook and Instagram, now work to append labels to images or videos created via AI.
Others, like LinkedIn, have added buttons allowing users to report AI-generated content.
Snap has banned wholly AI-generated content from its recommendation algorithm, while Spotify recently announced it had removed 50 million AI-generated tracks from its platform.
Ossman said Etsy would add a function similar to LinkedIn’s that makes it easier for users to report listings that include misleading AI imagery.
He also said Etsy would be using technology to identify misleading imagery and fraudulent listings, with the goal of expanding removals of illicit listings in the coming months.
“We’re actively working to address the questions AI raises for our marketplace,” Ossman said in the post.
“This work is hard, and we don’t have every answer today. But I believe this is an important moment for Etsy, and that these initial steps are putting us on the right path.”
Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.

A tsunami alert has been issued in Italy after a series of tremors was detected off the Mediterranean coast.
As many as 12 quakes were recorded with magnitudes of up to 5.0 near Sicily on Friday lunchtime, prompting precautionary evacuations of schools in Palermo and Messina.
An orange tsunami alert was issued for residents to vigilant and exercise caution around coastal areas as students left classes and public offices were abandoned, according to local media.
A courthouse was evacuated as far away as Trapani, on the west coast, while students and municipal workers vacated buildings in Lipari, an island between Sicily and mainland Italy.
The epicentre was less than 60 miles from Palermo, on the northern coastline, which has a population of 648,260 as the island’s capital.
Locals reported feeling tremors in Palermo, Patti, Licata, Capo dʿOrlando and Campofelice di Roccella. Licata is 180km from the epicentre.
The other 11 tremors all registered above 3.0-magnitude, officials said.
The United States Geological Survey recorded a 5.7 magnitude quake at a depth of 10km north of the island, occurring at 10:19am local time.
At the time of writing, there were no reports of injuries or damage to property.
Palermo mayor Roberto Lagalla said the authorities were closely monitoring an evolving situation.
“Currently, no reports of damage to people or property have been received, but we believe it is our duty to take all necessary measures to ensure the safety of our citizens,” he said in a statement.
“The possible evacuation of some public buildings is purely precautionary, dictated by the need to act promptly and prudently.”
He urged residents and people near the coast stay away from the sea and follow the instructions of the relevant authorities.
Did you feel the earthquake? Contact james.reynolds@independent.co.uk
The Sicilian city of Marsala and neighbouring towns were struck by a tornado earlier this month in what experts said was an almost unprecedented event for the Mediterranean island.
Vehicles were overturned and two people were seriously injured on October 9 as the whirlwind swept through, destroying a house and damaging a school and other buildings.
“It was almost like an American tornado, nothing this violent has been seen in living memory,” the head of Sicily's civil protection agency Salvatore Cocina told Reuters.
Early in September the agency issued a warning saying the sweltering summer had led to a buildup of heat that could trigger extreme weather events in autumn.

China’s domestic online beauty sales are falling as C-beauty companies are ramping up export efforts and moving into international retail channels. The gap suggests a deliberate pivot from C-beauty toward overseas growth, targeting the categories and regions that K-beauty has spent the past decade winning over.
According to Jefferies’ China online beauty tracker , the country recorded a 6% year-on-year cosmetics sales decline in September 2026. Skin care fell 6.1%, while color cosmetics went down 5.2%.
However, at the same time, data from the Korea International Trade Association (KITA) shows China climbing from seventh place to fifth in global cosmetics exports. The trade body says China’s color cosmetics exports amount to nearly three times that of Korea’s.
C-beauty company Proya, meanwhile, has opened a European Innovation Center Laboratory in France and has announced it will begin selling across 400 Ulta Beauty stores in the US next month.
“This Europe Innovation Center Laboratory connects the European and Chinese ecosystems to draw on combined strengths and create new innovation capabilities,” says Hou Juncheng, founder and chairman of Proya Cosmetics.
The center is not the first bridge between Chinese and European beauty. French ingredient suppliers have been actively pursuing partnerships with Chinese cosmetics brands, and many Chinese perfumers train in France. The country’s Cosmetic Valley, meanwhile, has set up a Shanghai-based fragrance and cosmetics embassy to encourage collaboration between the two markets . Chinese beauty brands are expanding overseas, targeting markets where K-beauty has established a strong presence.
With color cosmetics exports already outpacing Korea’s and a growing foothold in US and European retail, C-beauty appears to be borrowing the playbook that got K-beauty onto global shelves.
The September figures from Jefferies’ tracker show many multinational beauty giants experiencing declining figures in China. L’Oréal fell 5%, Estée Lauder 8%, Procter & Gamble 20%, Shiseido 24%, and LVMH 26%.
Beiersdorf and Galderma were the only multinationals to grow, supported by their Nivea and Cetaphil brands. At the brand level, dermatological skin care like CeraVe and Cetaphil grew (35% and 58%, respectively), while Bobbi Brown fell 31%. Among domestic players, Mao Geping grew 26%, and Proya grew 1%.
As demand becomes increasingly selective, and derma-brands gain ground, Jefferies’ findings show skin care and color cosmetics accounting for over 80% of China’s beauty market. Both categories initially gave rise to K-beauty.
According to KITA, China’s cosmetic exports reached ₩8.14 trillion (US$6.1 billion) from January to July 2026, up 24% from ₩6.55 trillion (US$4.9 billion) a year earlier. The figures lifted China to fifth in global export rankings, behind France in the lead and South Korea in second place.
In color cosmetics, China has already overtaken Korea. Exports of lip and eye makeup, powders, and nail products totaled ₩1.88 trillion (US$1.41 billion) from January to July, about 2.9 times Korea’s ₩644.7 billion (US$484 million).
From January to July 2026, China’s lip makeup exports were 1.7 times Korea’s, and its eye makeup exports were 3.5 times. China’s exports grew 17% to 33% across all four color cosmetics categories (lip, eye, powders, and nail products), while Korea’s lip makeup and nail product exports fell 15% and 15.6%, respectively. Proya is expanding its international presence with a new research laboratory in France.
According to The Asia Business Daily, Kecia Steelman, CEO of Ulta Beauty, raised C-beauty during the company’s 2026 Q2 fiscal earnings call. She is quoted as saying, “[We are launching] Proya, the number one skin care brand in China. So it’s not just about K-Beauty anymore.”
Proya’s US launch will be the first time a Chinese premium skin care brand joins Ulta’s online and physical networks at the same time. The rollout is planned for November this year, and with it, Proya says it is “moving beyond mere product export to brand globalization.”
To expand, the company says, “brands must not only enter overseas markets but also earn a permanent place in consumers’ daily skin care regimens and secure a voice within elite global beauty narratives.”
Securing that voice, Proya has inaugurated its Europe Innovation Center Laboratory in France, with a 450 square meter site containing 76 pieces of equipment and seven dedicated researchers. The lab will focus on research and innovation in skin longevity, biology, biotechnology, and sustainable ingredients.
The lab will collaborate with the Hangzhou Longwu center in China, which handles formulation, ingredients, safety, and efficacy, and the Shanghai center, which works on hair care and the scalp microbiome.
Proya’s international push comes after its namesake brand, which accounts for around 70% of group revenue, posted a 7% sales decline in H1 2026. The drop was the company’s first after years of uninterrupted growth since its 2017 Shanghai listing. Jefferies says the brand returned to 1% growth in September, but the overseas expansion appears partly aimed at offsetting soft momentum.

articles.title_orig: All lanes open after deadly crash in Durham creates severe delays on I-40, I-885 near RDU
articles.title_zh: All lanes open after deadly crash in Durham creates severe delays on I-40, I-885 near RDU
articles.content_orig:
A busy stretch of Interstate 40 East near Raleigh-Durham International Airport reopened Friday morning several hours after Durham police found a woman who was hit by multiple unknown vehicles.
Durham police said they responded to a call about a pedestrian being hit on I-40 near Davis Drive around 1:30 a.m. When they arrived, they found the woman dead and said she had been hit multiple times by unknown vehicles.
The eastbound lanes of I-40 were closed for a mile from Exit 280 at Davis Drive to Exit 281 to South Miami Boulevard. The severe delays extended onto Interstate 885 as well.
At 8 a.m., a lane had reopened on I-40 and traffic was flowing again. All lanes on I-40 reopened by 8:30 a.m.
Hours before the morning commute, WRAL Breaking News Tracker arrived before 4 a.m. to find multiple officers blocking the interstate for an investigation. Police would not let reporters near the scene.
WRAL's Shaun Gallagher arrived at 6 a.m. as the backup worsened. According to Gallagher, the miles of backups on the road resembled 8:30 a.m. rush hour instead of the usual 6 a.m. traffic.
Sky 5 flew over the delays at 7:15 a.m., showing miles and miles of traffic.
Police said they cannot release any other information about the investigation at this time.
